record.original_question: Let p be a prime, and P a finite p-group. (a) Suppose that P has an abelian subgroup of order pn. For which n does P necessarily have a normal abelian subgroup of order pn? (b) Suppose that P has an elementary abelian subgroup of order pn. For which n does P necessarily have a normal elementary abelian subgroup of order pn? It is easy to see that for p = 2, the answer to(b) is “yes” only for n = 1. The answer to both questions is “yes” for n < (p + 2)/2(G. G. Glauberman, J. Algebra, 319, no. 2(2008), 800–805), as well as for n ⩽ 5 when p ̸= 2(M. Konvisser, D. Jonah, J. Algebra, 34(1975), 309–330). The answer to both questions is “no” for n ⩾ (p+9)/2 when p ⩾ 5(for p ⩾ 7 due to G. Glauberman, Contemp. Math., 524(2010), 61–65; for p = 3, 5 due to Ya. G. Berkovich, J. Algebra, 248, no. 2(2002), 472–553). Thus, the only open cases for p ⩾ 5 are n = 6 for p = 5, and n = (p + 3)/2, (p + 5)/2, (p + 7)/2 for p > 5.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $p$ be a prime and let $P$ be a finite $p$-group. Recall that an abelian subgroup is called elementary abelian if every nonidentity element has order $p$.

(a) Determine the positive integers $n$ such that the following holds for every prime $p$ and every finite $p$-group $P$: if $P$ contains an abelian subgroup of order $p^n$, then $P$ contains a normal abelian subgroup of order $p^n$.

(b) Determine the positive integers $n$ such that the following holds for every prime $p$ and every finite $p$-group $P$: if $P$ contains an elementary abelian subgroup of order $p^n$, then $P$ contains a normal elementary abelian subgroup of order $p^n$.

It is known that for $p=2$, statement (b) holds only for $n=1$. For odd primes $p$, both statements are known to hold whenever $n<(p+2)/2$ and (for $p\neq 2$) whenever $n\le 5$, and both statements fail in general whenever $n\ge (p+9)/2$ and $p\ge 5$. The remaining unresolved cases are: $n=6$ when $p=5$, and $n=(p+3)/2,\,(p+5)/2,\,(p+7)/2$ when $p>5$. Resolve (a) and (b) in these remaining cases.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is a classical question on normal abelian/elementary abelian subgroups of finite p-groups. Bounds due to Glauberman, Konvisser–Jonah, and Berkovich settle the cases n < (p+2)/2 and n ≤ 5 (positive) and n ≥ (p+9)/2 for p ≥ 5 (negative). The intermediate cases (n=6 for p=5; n=(p+3)/2,(p+5)/2,(p+7)/2 for p>5) remain open according to the 2026 Kourovka Notebook listing, with no published full resolution found.

status_evidence.title: Glauberman, Large abelian subgroups of finite p-groups
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes the existence of normal abelian/elementary abelian subgroups of order p^n in p-groups containing such a subgroup, for n < (p+2)/2.

status_evidence.title: Glauberman, Centrally large subgroups and a theorem of Berkovich, Contemp. Math. 524 (2010)
status_evidence.snippet: Provides counterexamples for sufficiently large n when p ≥ 7.
status_evidence.claim: Negative answer for n ≥ (p+9)/2 when p ≥ 7.

status_evidence.title: Berkovich, On subgroups of finite p-groups, J. Algebra 248 (2002)
status_evidence.snippet: Counterexamples for primes p = 3, 5 in the corresponding range.
status_evidence.claim: Negative answer for p = 3, 5 in large n.

status_evidence.title: Kourovka Notebook (Unsolved Problems in Group Theory)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists the remaining open cases for n between (p+2)/2 and (p+9)/2.
status_evidence.claim: Problem listed as open in the unresolved range.
